items.followUp: A body moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a speed of 6 m/s. Find its centripetal acceleration.

rubric.why: Checks the defining direction of centripetal acceleration.
rubric.description: Defines centripetal acceleration as directed towards the centre of the circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the acceleration is directed towards the centre of the circle.

rubric.description: Gives the equation for centripetal acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing a = v²/r.

modelAnswer: Centripetal acceleration is the acceleration of a body moving in a circular path, directed towards the centre of the circle.
Its equation is a = v²/r, where v is the speed and r is the radius of the circular path.

items.followUp: Define momentum and write its SI unit.

rubric.description: Defines force as a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of force.

rubric.why: Checks the SI unit of force.
rubric.description: Names the newton as the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the unit is newton (N).

modelAnswer: A force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: A right-angled triangle has a base of 5 cm and a perpendicular of 12 cm. Find its hypotenuse.

rubric.why: Checks correct use of Pythagoras' theorem with the given dimensions converted to SI units.
rubric.description: Uses the Pythagorean relation for the hypotenuse.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation and substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated hypotenuse and its unit.
rubric.description: Finds the hypotenuse as 0.05 m (5 cm).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: base = 4 cm = 0.04 m; perpendicular = 3 cm = 0.03 m.
Formula: hypotenuse² = base² + perpendicular².
Substitution: hypotenuse = √[(0.04 m)² + (0.03 m)²] = 0.05 m.
Answer: The length of the hypotenuse is 0.05 m (5 cm).

items.followUp: What is a satellite? State one use of an artificial satellite.

rubric.why: Checks that GPS is identified as a satellite-based system.
rubric.description: States that GPS is a system that uses satellites orbiting the Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its use of satellites.

rubric.why: Checks the main purpose of GPS.
rubric.description: States that GPS helps determine the position or location of a receiver on Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it determines position or location.

modelAnswer: GPS (Global Positioning System) is a satellite-based navigation system.
It uses signals from satellites to determine the precise position or location of a receiver on Earth.

items.followUp: Define power and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of the unit watt in terms of work and time.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as one joule of work done per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 1 W = 1 J/s.

rubric.why: Checks the conversion from horsepower to watts.
rubric.description: States that one horsepower is equal to 746 watts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion.

modelAnswer: One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second (1 W = 1 J/s).
One horsepower = 746 watts.

items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and gives 350 J of useful output energy. Find its percentage efficiency.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of efficiency as a useful output-to-input ratio.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output energy (or work) divided by input energy (or work).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the correct ratio.

rubric.why: Checks the equation for percentage efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct percentage equation.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy (or work) to input energy (or work).
Percentage efficiency = (useful output energy ÷ input energy) × 100%.

items.followUp: Define density and calculate the density of a substance of mass 2 kg and volume 0.001 m³.

rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating density is mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: Checks the standard density value for gold.
rubric.description: Gives the density of gold as 19,300 kg/m³ (19.3 g/cm³).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent value with units.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass of a substance per unit volume.
The density of gold is 19,300 kg/m³ (or 19.3 g/cm³).

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the equation v = u + at.

rubric.why: Checks recognition that displacement is obtained from the area under the graph.
rubric.description: States that displacement is the area under the speed-time (velocity-time) graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying displacement with the graph area.

rubric.why: Checks the correct rectangle-plus-triangle area expression.
rubric.description: Writes displacement as the area of the rectangle plus the triangle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ut + ½(v − u)t.

rubric.why: Checks use of the acceleration relation to eliminate time.
rubric.description: Uses a = (v − u)/t, or its rearrangement, in the area equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration relation or rearrangement.

rubric.why: Checks the derived third equation of motion.
rubric.description: Obtains the third equation of motion.

modelAnswer: For uniform acceleration, let the initial velocity be u, final velocity be v, time be t and displacement be s.
Displacement is the area under the speed-time graph: s = area of rectangle + area of triangle.
s = ut + ½(v − u)t.
From the first equation of motion, a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting: s = u(v − u)/a + (v − u)²/(2a).
Multiplying by 2a and simplifying: 2as = 2u(v − u) + (v − u)² = v² − u².
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as.
